prompt: A triangle has angles measuring $90^\circ$, $45^\circ$, and $45^\circ$. Which name fits it BEST?
hint: One angle is exactly $90^\circ$ — what do we call a triangle with a square corner?

hints.text: One angle is exactly $90^\circ$ — what do we call a triangle with a square corner?
Two of the angles are equal ($45^\circ$ and $45^\circ$), which means two sides are equal too.
Right corner plus two equal angles makes it a right isosceles triangle.

explanation: A $90^\circ$ angle is a right angle, so this is a right triangle.
Two angles are the same size ($45^\circ$ and $45^\circ$), and equal angles sit across from equal sides, so two sides match — that is isosceles.
Scalene would mean no equal sides, and equilateral would need three $60^\circ$ angles, so neither fits.
The best name is a right isosceles triangle.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check the angle sum
steps: $90 + 45 + 45 = 180^\circ$, so these angles really can form a triangle.
Nothing is over $90^\circ$, so it is not obtuse.
